pr.title: fix(source): defer involved-sweep pr: cursors until delivery
pr.body:
Closes #98. Exactly-once on the involved-PR sweeps.

The involved-PR sweeps advanced their per-PR `pr:<scope>` cursor eagerly, before the engine confirmed delivery. A failed send moved the cursor past that PR's `updated_at`, so the next poll skipped it and the event was lost until the PR changed again (at-most-once).

### Change
The `pr:` cursor now gets the same deferral the snapshots already have: `diff_swept_prs` stashes the intended advance in `pending_pr_cursors`, and `commit_snapshots` flushes it only for scopes **not** in `failed_scopes`. So a scope whose delivery failed keeps its old cursor *and* old snapshot, and re-derives next poll — genuine exactly-once. Applied to both sweep-based sources, GitHub and Gitea.

### GitLab is unaffected
GitLab's involved-MR sweep has no per-PR cursor — it uses a global `mr_since` window plus the (already-deferred) snapshot for per-MR dedup, so there's no eager per-PR cursor to fix here. (The issue text mentioned it; this clarifies.)

### Tests
GitHub and Gitea each assert the `pr:` cursor is `None` after `poll()` alone and only advances after `commit_snapshots` with no failed scopes.

expected.description: The pr: cursor is staged even when process_pr swallowed a fetch failure, so the PR is skipped until it changes again and its event is lost.
